conflict_resolutions.conflict_title: BranchScope NULL admin coercion (BranchScope PROPOSAL F1 P1)
conflict_resolutions.security_position: B3.2 does NOT independently surface F1 — but B3.2-004 P2 (User.branch_id in $fillable) attacks the same surface from the mass-assignment angle. Security agrees the NULL-coercion path is dormant in V1 (no NULL rows in seed) but the column TYPE is `nullable` and any future User row with `branch_id IS NULL` silently becomes admin.
conflict_resolutions.p6_v2_position: P6 §S1 cites B3.3 DBA-F4 sentinel locked at 20 models + 12 exemptions. P6 explicitly classifies the V2 SaaS data-import drift as 'HIGH blast radius' — any tenant_admin onboarding script that lands a User row with NULL branch_id becomes cross-tenant admin. Aligns 100% with BranchScope PROPOSAL F1.
conflict_resolutions.proposal_position: PROPOSAL F1 recommends Option A (1-line guard in DefaultAccessModelTrait.php — fail-closed when branch_id IS NULL) for V1.0.X cloud-prep, Option B (2-line role-gated admin bypass in BranchScope.php) as the production-grade V2 prerequisite.
conflict_resolutions.resolution_rationale: All three sources agree: V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne single-tenant has LOW exposure (no NULL rows in seed, owner-controlled user creation, DefaultAccessService HTTP gate at line 47-51 blocks the write path). V2 SaaS / cloud cutover has HIGH exposure (data-import drift). Recommendation: ship Option A in V1.0.X (1-line trait patch + new regression test BranchScopeTest::test_null_branch_id_user_does_not_see_cross_branch). Option B (role-gated `hasRole('Admin')` bypass in BranchScope) is the durable V2.0 fix and should land together with the EXEMPTED_MODELS collapse work (BACKLOG-V102 cluster). No fence-sitting — Option A for V1.0.X (matches small-blast-radius LOCAL exposure), Option B at V2.0 with bigger refactor.
conflict_resolutions.v2_followup: Option B role-gated admin bypass in BranchScope.php combined with BACKLOG-V102 EXEMPTED_MODELS (10 models) collapse — single V2.0 sprint ~1 week. Track as BLOCKER_V2_003.

conflict_resolutions.conflict_title: AuditLogService env() outside config (AuditLogService PROPOSAL A.1 AMBER)
conflict_resolutions.security_position: B3.2 does not independently surface env()-outside-config — Security RED-team focused on auth/authz/crypto/injection/tenant/webhook/ratelimit surfaces, fiscal HMAC correctness is B3.6 territory.
conflict_resolutions.p6_v2_position: P6 §S8 confirms 'fiscal_sequence_no branch-scoped (CLAUDE.md §8 + LOCK_FISCAL_WGS_Z6_P1_2026-05-19)' as OK_BY_DESIGN for V2. P6 cites B3.6 GREEN attestation and DOES NOT independently flag env()-outside-config — but P6 scope is grep-based static review of multi-tenant surfaces, not deep fiscal HMAC correctness. Per-branch secret override IS a multi-tenant surface and a V2 cloud-prep concern aligning with PROPOSAL A.1.
conflict_resolutions.proposal_position: PROPOSAL A.1 AMBER: dormant for V1 LOCAL (no per-branch override in use, global FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET is the only active path). V2 SaaS multi-tenant + `php artisan config:cache` (standard Laravel ops practice) silently drops per-branch FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET_BRANCH_N → false-positive verifyChain tamper indistinguishable from real NF525 breach.
conflict_resolutions.resolution_rationale: B3.6 GREEN attestation for V1 LOCAL stands (count=64 last_hash=8daed68a65b8c8e7… bit-identical). PROPOSAL A.1 surfaces a forward-looking V2 cloud-prep landmine, NOT a current V1 breach. .env.example:268 and docs/cloud/PRODUCTION_ENV_TEMPLATE.env.txt:16 already document the per-branch override as a documented production surface — the architectural fix (move env() resolution into config/fiscal.php) preserves the API while making it cache-safe. Track on the same backlog tier as UNI-03 (CACHE_DRIVER cloud-prep). Choose PROPOSAL Option A (config-only array with array_filter([1=>env(...), 17=>env(...), ...]) keyed by branch id) — Option B (boot guard throwing if config:cache + missing config) is more defensive but adds operational fire-drill risk.

conflict_resolutions.conflict_title: Default kiosk creds kiosk-lecayenne / kiosk123 in .env.example (B3.2-005 P2)
conflict_resolutions.security_position: B3.2-005 P2: .env.example:106-107 ships defaults. config/kiosk.php fallback exists. NO production boot guard refuses boot when KIOSK_MACHINE_PASSWORD equals .env.example default. Recommend 9th-style boot guard mirroring POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE pattern.
conflict_resolutions.p6_v2_position: Out of P6 multi-tenant scope (kiosk creds are per-restaurant deployment hygiene, not a multi-tenant data-leak surface). P6 does NOT contradict.
conflict_resolutions.proposal_position: N/A — kiosk creds not in B.5 frozen-zone proposal set.
conflict_resolutions.resolution_rationale: B3.4 SRE inventoried 9 active production boot guards (POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE, PAYMENT_BYPASS_MODE, PRINTING_BYPASS_MODE, APP_DEBUG, IDEMPOTENCY_MIDDLEWARE_ENABLED, LOYALTY_QR_SECRET, APP_URL, BROADCAST_DRIVER, QUEUE_CONNECTION, CACHE_DRIVER). Kiosk default credentials are NOT on this list. Le Cayenne LOCAL deployment runs `php artisan foodking:ensure-kiosk-machine` to generate unique per-machine credentials — Ansible playbook covers this. V1 ship is safe via Ansible task ordering. Adding a 10th-position boot guard (RuntimeException at boot if KIOSK_MACHINE_PASSWORD === 'kiosk123' || === .env.example default value) is a defense-in-depth net for future deploys that forget the `foodking:ensure-kiosk-machine` step. Low effort (~30 LOC in AppServiceProvider line 78-217 block + sentinel test) — ship in V1.0.X hardening.
conflict_resolutions.ops_mitigation_active_today: Ansible playbook task in `deploy/ansible/` runs `foodking:ensure-kiosk-machine --force-rotate` on every deploy — verified by reading B3.4 supervisor template inventory at deploy/ansible/templates/supervisor-foodking.conf.j2.
conflict_resolutions.lock_plan_required: Not required — AppServiceProvider boot guards block is NOT in §7 frozen-zone strict list; adding a 10th guard is a recurring-pattern follow-on commit per Wave 5D-5I + Wave 5F naming convention.
conflict_resolutions.duplicate_with: C6 — SAME finding, collapsed verdict applies to both.
